title: Taking Managed Instances through design, security and rollout
question: Tell me about a time you drove a technical initiative that spanned multiple teams.

situation: AWS launched Managed Instances for Lambda so customers could run functions on EC2 infrastructure with native scaling and cost efficiency. As part of the Code Management & Optimization team, our service had to support function packaging, artifact storage and optimisation for this new execution tier.
task: I took ownership of my team's initiative: leading the high-level design and the operational readiness review, driving the multi-service deployment, and acting as the primary technical contact for the control plane and data plane partner teams.
action: Architectural steering and pivot: when the security requirements shifted mid-project from S3 KMS encryption to dedicated artifact encryption at rest, I identified early that full alignment with Lambda On-Demand was no longer possible. I re-architected the design and rewrote the core components before our team could become a blocker.

Cross-service delivery: I orchestrated end-to-end integration and a zero-customer-impact deployment across several control plane and data plane dependencies, establishing rigorous validation pipelines along the way.
result: All of the team's code changes and operational readiness requirements landed on schedule with zero customer impact, giving Lambda Managed Instances seamless support from our service.

challenge: Adapting to a major architectural shift mid-development. Realising we could not fully mirror Lambda On-Demand, because of the new mandatory artifact encryption-at-rest requirement, meant revisiting our fundamental data flows and rewriting a large part of the codebase under a tight timeline.
hardestBug: Cross-service failure scenarios during joint testing. Our code interacted with several external control and data plane services, so I regularly had to run exhaustive isolation tests to pinpoint edge-case failures and demonstrate to partner teams that the fault lay in their service layer.
differently: I would push for an explicit early audit of emerging security and compliance requirements, rather than assuming a new feature paradigm can align fully with legacy execution patterns like Lambda On-Demand.
aboutYourself: I have the technical depth and the confidence to drive major architectural decisions across organisational boundaries. It showed me I can guide multi-team initiatives, challenge flawed assumptions and pivot a high-level design without giving up the timeline.
enjoyed: Mapping out the end-to-end system design, finding the subtle edge cases, and reasoning through complex multi-service interactions across the AWS control and data plane ecosystem.
